text:
drew: follow-up on the quant profiles RFC: proposal to perform all profile merging at compile/build time. runtime should receive a single pre-flattened profile (v2) per model bundle and only perform lane selection, not merges. pros/cons?

nina: in favor of simplifying runtime path. my worry is per-customer tuning for Dedicated/Privatehow do we let customers override without forcing recompile?

drew: idea: allow a tiny override manifest applied during deploy on the host (not at token time). runtime will validate and enforce handshake compatibility but won't merge complex rules on the fly.

kevin: does this kill per-request precision negotiation (client explicitly asks for int8 vs fp8)?

alice: we planned to deprecate live negotiation because it explodes state and testing. instead we accept a "precision-hint" header and runtime maps to the closest lane in the flattened profile. no dynamic profile merging.

sara: telemetry-wise we must tag every inference with the profile_id and compile_hash so we can trace quality regressions back to the compiled profile. otherwise investigating regressions will be a nightmare.

drew: agreed. add metadata fields: profile_id, source_tag, compile_hash on the request/response envelope. pipeline needs to ingest them.

ben: can you paste an example v2 profile we expect to embed?

drew: ```
# quant_profile v2 example
{
  "profile_id": "qp-2026-03-21-a",
  "compile_hash": "sha256:ef12...",
  "lanes": [
    {"name":"fp8-lowlat","bit":"fp8","est_latency_ms":3},
    {"name":"int8-cost","bit":"int8","est_latency_ms":6},
    {"name":"4bit-slow","bit":"4bit","est_latency_ms":8}
  ],
  "defaults": {"fallback":"int8-cost","safety_threshold":"deg_score<0.02"}
}
```

nina: runtime should reject mismatched compile_hash at handshake. fail fast with clear error and suggested compatible lanes.

drew: yes  handshake returns 412 with a small compatibility payload listing accepted lanes and required recompile/override steps.

kevin: need a compatibility mode for older clients that expect runtime merging. make it opt-in per deployment only.

alice: +1 but keep it off by default. ops should use it only in short transition windows. also we'll need extra tests for that mode.

sara: ops Q: how big will these flattened profiles be? care about bundle size and memory.

drew: profiles themselves are tiny (KBs). calibration artifacts (tables/tensors) will remain separate and referenced by hash to avoid bundle bloat.

ops-bot: checklist: canary must include telemetry tags, feature-flag rollout, alert when handshake-mismatch-rate > 0.5%

ben: can the build step include a lint that flags dangerous drops (e.g., fp8 -> 4bit) and require explicit opt-in?

drew: yes. compile-time linter will emit warnings and make aggressive downbitting require an explicit "allow_downbit": true in the override manifest.

nina: also need rollback semantics for overrides without recompile. can we support swapping override manifest and restarting without a full recompile?

drew: yes, override manifests are separate artifacts referenced by hash and can be swapped at deploy-time; restart picks up new manifest. we'll document the restart/rollback steps.

kevin: i'll draft the handshake error payload and the compat flag PR. @eng-runtime please review after I open the PR.

alice: i'll update telemetry schemas and add a small backfill job to annotate recent logs with profile_id where missing.

sara: timeline? aim for a canary next sprint?

drew: schedule: PRs this week, internal canary next sprint, 2-week canary, then gradual rollout.

kevin: sounds good.

alice: ack.

nina: ack.

sara: ack.
